source.name: NASA Technical Paper 1907
source.citation: S. Gordon, Thermodynamic and Transport Combustion Properties of Hydrocarbons with Air, Part II: Compositions Corresponding to Kelvin Temperature Schedules in Part I

transcription: Rows were transcribed from NASA TP-1907 Table 11.3E for H/C=2.000, F/A=0.084535, equivalence ratio=1.250, chemical equivalence ratio=1.2496, dry air, 101.325 kPa. The printed gas and condensed values sum to one within five-decimal rounding only when C(gr) is included; the frozen contract therefore models them as system-total mole fractions. NASA considered 55 gases and 3 condensed phases before printing its selected columns. Tests never download or re-run NASA software.
